Affinity Colocation

1. What is Affinity Colocation?
  • Affinity colocation ensures that related data is stored on the same node;
  • For example, all orders belonging to a customer can be colocated with that customer's record;
  • This means queries and computations that access related data don't need network hops — everything is local;
  • Without colocation, a join between Customer and Order tables would require shuffling data across the network;
2. How does it work?
  • Ignite uses the affinity key to determine which partition (and therefore which node) a data entry belongs to;
  • By default, the entire cache key is used as the affinity key;
  • You can designate a specific field of the key as the affinity key using the @AffinityKeyMapped annotation;
  • All entries with the same affinity key value end up in the same partition on the same node;
3. Configuring Affinity Colocation
  • Using @AffinityKeyMapped annotation: 
    public class OrderKey {
    @AffinityKeyMapped
    private int customerId;  // orders colocated by customerId
    private int orderId;

    // constructor, getters, equals, hashCode...
}
  • Using AffinityKey wrapper: 
    // Key: orderId, Affinity key: customerId
AffinityKey<Integer> key = new AffinityKey<>(orderId, customerId);
orderCache.put(key, orderValue);
  • Via SQL: 
    CREATE TABLE Orders (
    orderId INT,
    customerId INT,
    amount DECIMAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (orderId, customerId)
) WITH "affinityKey=customerId,cache_name=OrderCache,backups=1";
4. When should you use Affinity Colocation?
  • When you frequently join or cross-reference two caches/tables (e.g., Customer + Orders, Product + Reviews);
  • When you run collocated compute tasks that need to process related data locally;
  • When you want to avoid the overhead of distributed joins;
5. Impact on SQL Joins
  • If two tables are colocated on the same affinity key, Ignite can perform the join locally on each node — this is called a colocated join;
  • If tables are not colocated, Ignite must perform a non-colocated (distributed) join, which sends data across the network and is much slower;
  • Non-colocated joins must be explicitly enabled: 
    SqlFieldsQuery query = new SqlFieldsQuery("SELECT ... FROM A JOIN B ON ...");
query.setDistributedJoins(true);
